newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian banker says supplementary budget needed.
newsitem.headline: Italian banker says supplementary budget needed.

text.p: The President of the Italian Banking Association (ABI), Tancredi Bianchi, said on Monday that Italy needed a supplementary budget worth up to 30 trillion lire to qualify for a single European currency.
"With an extra effort, worth a maximum of 20-30 trillion lire we will enter Europe," Bianchi told Reuters.

The Italian government has said that it may have to ram through a supplementary budget early in 1997 to keep alive Italy's quest to cut the public sector deficit to three percent of gross domestic product (GDP).
The 1997 budget, approved at the end of last year, aims to slice 62.5 trillion lire from the public sector deficit.

"In 1997 public accounts will go better than in 1996, but that depends on how the 62.5 trillion budget goes. If it is 80 percent successful, the accounts will improve. If it is only 50 percent successful, then they won't (improve)," he said.
He said the public sector surplus of two trillion lire announced by the treasury for January "could just be a one-off, we will have to see," he added.
Interest rates and the pace of progress with the government's privatisation program would have an impact on public accounts in 1997.

Bianchi said there was limited scope for further interest rate cuts. "But even if interest rates stand still, we save, given that we are on average three percentage points below 1996 levels," he said.
He estimated the savings on interest payments amounted to around 20 trillion lire in 1997.

Privatisations were crucial. "Without significant privatisations we will not be able to maintain any of the parameters. Only by privatising will we be able to succeed and make rates come down. This is the main point of difficulty," he said.
